methods.label: Count by a chosen side
methods.explanation:
Any two distinct points determine exactly two equilateral triangles, one on each side of the line joining them. There are \(\binom{9}{2}=36\) pairs of polygon vertices, so choosing a pair and an equilateral completion gives
\[
2\binom{9}{2}=72
\]
counts. Every triangle requested in the question appears in this count because it contains at least one such pair.

A triangle with exactly two polygon vertices is counted once. A triangle with three polygon vertices is counted three times, once for each side. We therefore need to identify the latter triangles.

Consecutive vertices of the regular nonagon are \(360^\circ/9=40^\circ\) apart about its center. An equilateral triangle on the same circumcircle has three \(60^\circ\) inscribed angles, so each arc between consecutive triangle vertices measures \(120^\circ\). Its vertices must therefore occur every three polygon vertices. The only such triangles are
\[
A_1A_4A_7,\qquad A_2A_5A_8,\qquad A_3A_6A_9.
\]
Each was counted three times and should remain once, so we remove two counts for each. The number of distinct triangles is
\[
72-2\cdot3=\boxed{66},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
methods.levelReason: This uses elementary combinations, multiplicity correction, and school geometry about regular polygons and inscribed angles.

review.mathematicalCheck: The 36 vertex pairs yield 72 pair-triangle incidences. An inscribed equilateral triangle requires three 120-degree arcs, so exactly three triangles use three nonagon vertices. These contribute three counts each; all other requested triangles contribute one. Thus the total is 72−2·3=66.
